chapters.narration: This open-access paper is a review, not a new patient experiment. Its published Figure One maps possible ways microfluidic systems might detect respiratory viruses.
headline: PRIMARY SOURCE
chapters.evidence_caption: Overview of microfluidic methods used for detection of respiratory viruses. Various collected samples (genetic materials or direct respiratory virus particles in body fluids) can be detected using microfluidic-based detection systems that can contain antibodies, aptamers, magnetic beads, nanoparticles, or enzymes

chapters.narration: Sample preparation is upstream of detection. A swab, saliva specimen, or other fluid must be handled before a device can produce an interpretable signal.
headline: SAMPLE HANDLING

chapters.narration: Some methods seek viral particles or antigens. Others search for viral nucleic acid. Those distinct targets create very different assay architectures.
headline: TARGET SELECTION

chapters.narration: The authors' original Figure One connects sample, sensing elements, and transduction. These are alternatives, not proof that one fabricated chip performs every assay.
headline: THE PUBLISHED SCHEMATIC
chapters.evidence_caption: Overview of microfluidic methods used for detection of respiratory viruses. Various collected samples (genetic materials or direct respiratory virus particles in body fluids) can be detected using microfluidic-based detection systems that can contain antibodies, aptamers, magnetic beads, nanoparticles, or enzymes

chapters.narration: An antibody, aptamer, magnetic bead, nanoparticle, or enzyme can form part of the sensing strategy. Specificity still depends on careful recognition chemistry.
headline: BINDING CHEMISTRY

chapters.narration: In optical schemes, changes in light are translated into a readout. The moving traces here explain the idea; they are not experimental results.
headline: OPTICAL DETECTION

chapters.narration: Electrical and electrochemical methods use different signal pathways and calibration requirements. A visually convincing waveform alone cannot establish diagnostic accuracy.
headline: ELECTRICAL TRANSDUCTION

chapters.narration: The scientific contribution is a critical map of detection technologies. Clinical validity requires sensitivity, specificity, controls, and verification in a defined population.
headline: A REVIEW IS NOT A TRIAL
